body.en: Unit 4 connects the analytical derivative to dynamic physical phenomena: rectilinear motion of particles, geometric systems undergoing simultaneous time-varying changes (related rates), tangent line linear approximations with concavity-based error analysis, and the rigorous evaluation of indeterminate limits via L'Hôpital's Rule.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Straight-Line Motion & Rates of Change in Context

body.en: In rectilinear kinematics, a particle's motion along a coordinate axis is governed by position s(t), velocity v(t) = s'(t), acceleration a(t) = v'(t) = s''(t), and speed |v(t)|.

label.ar: ● Rectilinear Motion Taxonomy & Sign Analysis (الوحدة ٤ · التطبيقات السياقية والفيزيائية للاشتقاق)

body.en:
Let \(s(t)\) represent the position of a particle along a line at time \(t\):

  1. Velocity: \(v(t) = s'(t) = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{s(t+\Delta t) - s(t)}{\Delta t}\). The sign of \(v(t)\) dictates direction: \(v(t) > 0 \implies\) moving right/up; \(v(t) < 0 \implies\) moving left/down; \(v(t) = 0 \implies\) instantaneously at rest.
  2. Acceleration: \(a(t) = v'(t) = s''(t)\). Measures the instantaneous rate of change of velocity.
  3. Displacement vs. Total Distance Traveled: Over an interval \([t_1, t_2]\): \[ \text{Displacement} = \Delta s = s(t_2) - s(t_1) = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} v(t)\,dt \] \[ \text{Total Distance} = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} |v(t)|\,dt \]

label.en: ● Theorem & Proof: Speeding Up vs. Slowing Down
label.ar: ● مبرهنة & برهان: Speeding Up vs. Slowing Down

body.en:
Theorem: The speed \(S(t) = |v(t)|\) of a moving particle is increasing (speeding up) when \(v(t)\) and \(a(t)\) have the same sign (\(v(t)a(t) > 0\)). The speed is decreasing (slowing down) when \(v(t)\) and \(a(t)\) have opposite signs (\(v(t)a(t) < 0\)).

Analytical Proof: Express speed as \(S(t) = \sqrt{v(t)^2}\). Differentiating with respect to \(t\) using the Chain Rule: \[ \frac{dS}{dt} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{v(t)^2}} \cdot \frac{d}{dt}[v(t)^2] = \frac{1}{2|v(t)|} \cdot 2v(t)v'(t) = \frac{v(t)a(t)}{|v(t)|} \quad (\text{for } v(t) \neq 0) \] Since \(|v(t)| > 0\) for all non-zero velocities, the algebraic sign of \(\frac{dS}{dt}\) is identical to the sign of the product \(v(t)a(t)\):

  • If \(v(t) > 0\) and \(a(t) > 0\), then \(v(t)a(t) > 0 \implies \frac{dS}{dt} > 0\) (speed increasing).
  • If \(v(t) < 0\) and \(a(t) < 0\), then \(v(t)a(t) > 0 \implies \frac{dS}{dt} > 0\) (speed increasing).
  • If \(v(t)\) and \(a(t)\) have opposing signs, \(v(t)a(t) < 0 \implies \frac{dS}{dt} < 0\) (speed decreasing). \(\blacksquare\)
body.ar:
Theorem: The speed \(S(t) = |v(t)|\) of a moving particle is increasing (speeding up) عندما \(v(t)\) and \(a(t)\) have the same sign (\(v(t)a(t) > 0\)). The speed is decreasing (slowing down) عندما \(v(t)\) and \(a(t)\) have opposite signs (\(v(t)a(t) < 0\)).

Analytical برهان: Express speed as \(S(t) = \sqrt{v(t)^2}\). Differentiating بالنسبة إلى \(t\) using the Chain Rule: \[ \frac{dS}{dt} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{v(t)^2}} \cdot \frac{d}{dt}[v(t)^2] = \frac{1}{2|v(t)|} \cdot 2v(t)v'(t) = \frac{v(t)a(t)}{|v(t)|} \quad (\text{for } v(t) \neq 0) \] Since \(|v(t)| > 0\) for all non-zero velocities, the algebraic sign of \(\frac{dS}{dt}\) is identical to the sign of the product \(v(t)a(t)\):

  • If \(v(t) > 0\) and \(a(t) > 0\), then \(v(t)a(t) > 0 \implies \frac{dS}{dt} > 0\) (speed increasing).
  • If \(v(t) < 0\) and \(a(t) < 0\), then \(v(t)a(t) > 0 \implies \frac{dS}{dt} > 0\) (speed increasing).
  • If \(v(t)\) and \(a(t)\) have opposing signs, \(v(t)a(t) < 0 \implies \frac{dS}{dt} < 0\) (speed decreasing). \(\blacksquare\)

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Unit 4 · Contextual Applications of Differentiation)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Unit 4 · Contextual Applications of Differentiation)

body.en:
Why Differentiability Implies Continuity & How Implicit Differentiation Works: Notice that for \(x \ne a\), we can write \(f(x) - f(a) = \dfrac{f(x) - f(a)}{x - a}\cdot (x - a)\). Taking the limit as \(x \to a\) by the Product Law gives:

\[ \lim_{x \to a} \bigl(f(x) - f(a)\bigr) = f'(a)\cdot 0 = 0 \implies \lim_{x \to a} f(x) = f(a) \]

Similarly, when differentiating an implicit relation \(F(x, y) = c\) with respect to \(x\), \(y = y(x)\) is an inner function of \(x\). By the Chain Rule, \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\bigl[y^n\bigr] = ny^{n-1}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\), and for product terms \(\dfrac{d}{dx}[xy] = y + x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).
body.ar:
Why Differentiability Implies Continuity & How Implicit Differentiation Works: Notice that for \(x \ne a\), we can write \(f(x) - f(a) = \dfrac{f(x) - f(a)}{x - a}\cdot (x - a)\). Taking the النهاية as \(x \to a\) by the Product Law gives:

\[ \lim_{x \to a} \bigl(f(x) - f(a)\bigr) = f'(a)\cdot 0 = 0 \implies \lim_{x \to a} f(x) = f(a) \]

Similarly, عندما differentiating an implicit relation \(F(x, y) = c\) بالنسبة إلى \(x\), \(y = y(x)\) is an inner الدالة of \(x\). By the Chain Rule, \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\bigl[y^n\bigr] = ny^{n-1}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\), and for product terms \(\dfrac{d}{dx}[xy] = y + x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

label.en: Level 1 (Foundations) — Worked Example · Complete Kinematic Analysis
label.ar: Level 1 (Foundations) — مثال محلول · Complete Kinematic Analysis

body.en:
Problem: A particle moves along the x-axis with position \(s(t) = t^3 - 9t^2 + 24t - 5\) for \(t \ge 0\).

  1. Find all times when the particle is at rest and determine the intervals when it moves left.
  2. At \(t = 3\), determine whether the particle's speed is increasing or decreasing with justification.
  3. Calculate the total distance traveled by the particle over \([0, 5]\).

Solution:

  1. \(v(t) = s'(t) = 3t^2 - 18t + 24 = 3(t^2 - 6t + 8) = 3(t - 2)(t - 4)\). The particle is at rest when \(v(t) = 0 \implies \mathbf{t = 2}\) and \(\mathbf{t = 4}\). Testing signs: \(v(t) < 0\) on \((2, 4)\). The particle moves left on \((2, 4)\).
  2. Evaluate velocity and acceleration at \(t = 3\): \[ v(3) = 3(3-2)(3-4) = -3 < 0 \] \[ a(t) = v'(t) = 6t - 18 \implies a(3) = 6(3) - 18 = 0 \] Since acceleration is zero, the speed is neither increasing nor decreasing at the instantaneous inflection point \(t = 3\). At \(t = 1\): \(v(1) = 3(-1)(-3) = 9 > 0\) and \(a(1) = 6(1)-18 = -12 < 0\); since \(v(1)\) and \(a(1)\) have opposite signs, speed is decreasing at \(t = 1\).
  3. Total distance traveled on \([0, 5]\) requires splitting at turning points \(t = 2\) and \(t = 4\): \[ s(0) = -5, \quad s(2) = 8 - 36 + 48 - 5 = 15 \] \[ s(4) = 64 - 144 + 96 - 5 = 11, \quad s(5) = 125 - 225 + 120 - 5 = 15 \] \[ \text{Total Distance} = |s(2) - s(0)| + |s(4) - s(2)| + |s(5) - s(4)| = |15 - (-5)| + |11 - 15| + |15 - 11| = 20 + 4 + 4 = \mathbf{28}. \]
body.ar:
Problem: A particle moves along the x-axis with position \(s(t) = t^3 - 9t^2 + 24t - 5\) for \(t \ge 0\).

  1. Find all times عندما the particle is at rest and حدّد intervals عندما it moves left.
  2. At \(t = 3\), حدّد ما إذا كان the particle's speed is increasing or decreasing with justification.
  3. Calculate the total distance traveled by the particle over \([0, 5]\).

Solution:

  1. \(v(t) = s'(t) = 3t^2 - 18t + 24 = 3(t^2 - 6t + 8) = 3(t - 2)(t - 4)\). The particle is at rest عندما \(v(t) = 0 \implies \mathbf{t = 2}\) and \(\mathbf{t = 4}\). Testing signs: \(v(t) < 0\) on \((2, 4)\). The particle moves left on \((2, 4)\).
  2. Evaluate velocity and acceleration at \(t = 3\): \[ v(3) = 3(3-2)(3-4) = -3 < 0 \] \[ a(t) = v'(t) = 6t - 18 \implies a(3) = 6(3) - 18 = 0 \] Since acceleration is zero, the speed is neither increasing nor decreasing at the instantaneous نقطة الانعطاف \(t = 3\). At \(t = 1\): \(v(1) = 3(-1)(-3) = 9 > 0\) and \(a(1) = 6(1)-18 = -12 < 0\); since \(v(1)\) and \(a(1)\) have opposite signs, speed is decreasing at \(t = 1\).
  3. Total distance traveled on \([0, 5]\) requires splitting at turning points \(t = 2\) and \(t = 4\): \[ s(0) = -5, \quad s(2) = 8 - 36 + 48 - 5 = 15 \] \[ s(4) = 64 - 144 + 96 - 5 = 11, \quad s(5) = 125 - 225 + 120 - 5 = 15 \] \[ \text{Total Distance} = |s(2) - s(0)| + |s(4) - s(2)| + |s(5) - s(4)| = |15 - (-5)| + |11 - 15| + |15 - 11| = 20 + 4 + 4 = \mathbf{28}. \]

label.en: Worked Example \(B\) — Unit 4 · Contextual Applications of Differentiation (Easy Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(B\) — Unit 4 · Contextual Applications of Differentiation (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): A rectangular garden has a length that is twice its width. If the perimeter of the garden is 36 meters, what is the width of the garden?

Step-by-Step Solution: Let the width of the garden be \( w \) meters. According to the problem, the length is twice the width, so the length is \( l = 2w \) meters. The formula for the perimeter of a rectangle is \( P = 2(l + w) \). We are given that the perimeter is 36 meters. So, we can set up the equation: \( 36 = 2(2w + w) \). Simplifying the equation: \( 36 = 2(3w) \) \( 36 = 6w \). To find the width, divide both sides by 6: \( w = \frac{36}{6} \) \( w = 6 \). Therefore, the width of the garden is 6 meters. Common misconceptions: - Confusing length and width: If one assumed length was width, they might get \( 36 = 2(w + 2w) \), which is the same equation. - Incorrect perimeter formula: Using \( P = l \times w \) would lead to \( 36 = 2w \times w = 2w^2 \), so \( w^2 = 18 \), and \( w = \sqrt{18} \), which is not among the options. - Calculation error: Dividing 36 by 3 instead of 6 would lead to a width of 12 meters.
body.ar:
Problem (Easy): A rectangular garden has a length that is twice its width. If the المحيط of the garden is 36 meters, what is the width of the garden?

Step-by-Step الحل: Let the width of the garden be \( w \) meters. According to the problem, the length is twice the width, so the length is \( l = 2w \) meters. The الصيغة for the المحيط of a rectangle is \( P = 2(l + w) \). We are بما أن the المحيط is 36 meters. So, we can set up the المعادلة: \( 36 = 2(2w + w) \). Simplifying the المعادلة: \( 36 = 2(3w) \) \( 36 = 6w \). To أوجد width, divide both sides by 6: \( w = \frac{36}{6} \) \( w = 6 \). وبالتالي, the width of the garden is 6 meters. Common misconceptions: - Confusing length and width: If one assumed length was width, they might get \( 36 = 2(w + 2w) \), which is the same المعادلة. - Incorrect المحيط الصيغة: Using \( P = l \times w \) would lead to \( 36 = 2w \times w = 2w^2 \), so \( w^2 = 18 \), and \( w = \sqrt{18} \), which is not among the options. - Calculation error: Dividing 36 by 3 instead of 6 would lead to a width of 12 meters.

label.en: ⚠️ Common Exam Traps — Unit 4 · Contextual Applications of Differentiation
label.ar: ⚠️ أخطاء شائعة في الاختبار — Unit 4 · Contextual Applications of Differentiation

body.en:
1. Premature L'Hôpital's Rule Application: On College Board AP Calculus AB, applying L'Hôpital's Rule to \(\lim_{x \to 4} \dfrac{g(x)}{h(x)}\) when the fraction is not an indeterminate form \(0/0\) or \(\infty/\infty\) produces completely false limits. Always verify \(g(4) = 0\) and \(h(4) = 0\) explicitly first.

2. Parametric Second Derivative Trap: For parametric curves \((x(t), y(t))\), \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{\frac{d}{dt}(dy/dx)}{dx/dt}\), never \(\dfrac{d^2y/dt^2}{d^2x/dt^2}\).
body.ar:
1. Premature L'Hôpital's Rule Application: On College Board AP التفاضل والتكامل AB, applying L'Hôpital's Rule to \(\lim_{x \to 4} \dfrac{g(x)}{h(x)}\) عندما the fraction is not an indeterminate form \(0/0\) or \(\infty/\infty\) produces completely false النهايات. Always verify \(g(4) = 0\) and \(h(4) = 0\) explicitly first.

2. Parametric Second المشتقة Trap: For parametric curves \((x(t), y(t))\), \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{\frac{d}{dt}(dy/dx)}{dx/dt}\), never \(\dfrac{d^2y/dt^2}{d^2x/dt^2}\).

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

A particle moves along a line with position \(s(t) = 2t^3 - 15t^2 + 24t + 10\). Determine the open intervals on \(t > 0\) during which the particle is speeding up.
question.ar:
Level 1 · Foundations

A particle moves along a line with position \(s(t) = 2t^3 - 15t^2 + 24t + 10\). حدّد open intervals on \(t > 0\) during which the particle is speeding up.

solution.en:
Find \(v(t)\) and \(a(t)\): \[ v(t) = 6t^2 - 30t + 24 = 6(t^2 - 5t + 4) = 6(t - 1)(t - 4) \] \[ a(t) = 12t - 30 = 6(2t - 5) \] Critical time points: \(t = 1\), \(t = 2.5\), \(t = 4\). Construct sign chart:

  • On \((0, 1)\): \(v(t) > 0\), \(a(t) < 0\) (opposite signs \(\implies\) slowing down).
  • On \((1, 2.5)\): \(v(t) < 0\), \(a(t) < 0\) (same sign \(\implies\) speeding up).
  • On \((2.5, 4)\): \(v(t) < 0\), \(a(t) > 0\) (opposite signs \(\implies\) slowing down).
  • On \((4, \infty)\): \(v(t) > 0\), \(a(t) > 0\) (same sign \(\implies\) speeding up).

The particle is speeding up on \((1, 2.5) \cup (4, \infty)\).

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Related Rates of Change

body.en: In related rates problems, multiple geometric quantities vary simultaneously with respect to time t. Differentiating the underlying constraint equation implicitly yields a linear relationship among their instantaneous rates.
body.ar: In related rates problems, multiple geometric quantities vary simultaneously بالنسبة إلى time t. Differentiating the underlying constraint المعادلة implicitly yields a linear relationship among their instantaneous rates.

label.ar: ● The 5-Step Related Rates Protocol (الوحدة ٤ · التطبيقات السياقية والفيزيائية للاشتقاق)

body.en:
1. Diagram & Variables: Sketch the geometric system, assign variables to all dynamic quantities, and note constants (dimensions that do not change with time).
  2. Identify Given and Target Rates: Express given rates as time derivatives (e.g., \(\frac{dV}{dt} = 4\text{ m}^3/\text{min}\)) and identify the target rate (e.g., \(\left.\frac{dh}{dt}\right|_{h=3}\)).
  3. Governing Constraint Equation: Formulate an equation relating the variables (Pythagorean theorem, trigonometric ratios, similar triangles, volume formulas). If necessary, eliminate auxiliary variables using geometric proportions before differentiating.
  4. Differentiate with Respect to Time: Apply the Chain Rule implicitly: \(\frac{d}{dt}[y^2] = 2y\frac{dy}{dt}\), \(\frac{d}{dt}[r^2 h] = 2rh\frac{dr}{dt} + r^2\frac{dh}{dt}\). Never substitute instantaneous values before differentiating.
  5. Instantaneous Evaluation & Units: Substitute known instantaneous values and solve algebraically for the target rate, specifying complete dimensional units.
body.ar:
1. Diagram & المتغيرات: Sketch the geometric system, assign المتغيرات to all dynamic quantities, and note constants (dimensions that do not change with time).
  2. Identify المعطيات and Target Rates: Express المعطيات rates as time المشتقات (e.g., \(\frac{dV}{dt} = 4\text{ m}^3/\text{min}\)) and identify the target rate (e.g., \(\left.\frac{dh}{dt}\right|_{h=3}\)).
  3. Governing Constraint المعادلة: Formulate an المعادلة relating the المتغيرات (Pythagorean المبرهنة, trigonometric ratios, similar triangles, الحجم الصيغ). If necessary, eliminate auxiliary المتغيرات using geometric proportions before differentiating.
  4. Differentiate بالنسبة إلى Time: Apply the Chain Rule implicitly: \(\frac{d}{dt}[y^2] = 2y\frac{dy}{dt}\), \(\frac{d}{dt}[r^2 h] = 2rh\frac{dr}{dt} + r^2\frac{dh}{dt}\). Never عوّض instantaneous values before differentiating.
  5. Instantaneous Evaluation & Units: عوّض known instantaneous values and solve algebraically for the target rate, specifying complete dimensional units.

label.en: Level 2 (Medium) — Worked Example · Conical Water Reservoir
label.ar: Level 2 (Medium) — مثال محلول · Conical Water Reservoir

body.en:
Problem: An inverted conical tank has height \(H = 12\text{ m}\) and top radius \(R = 4\text{ m}\). Water is pumped into the tank at a constant rate of \(3\text{ m}^3/\text{min}\). How fast is the water level rising when the water depth is \(h = 6\text{ m}\)?

Solution:

  1. Relate \(r\) and \(h\): By similar right triangles in the vertical cross section: \[ \frac{r}{h} = \frac{R}{H} = \frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3} \implies r = \frac{1}{3}h \]
  2. Express Volume in terms of \(h\) alone: \[ V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi \left(\frac{1}{3}h\right)^2 h = \frac{\pi}{27}h^3 \]
  3. Differentiate implicitly with respect to \(t\): \[ \frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{\pi}{27} \cdot 3h^2 \frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{\pi h^2}{9} \frac{dh}{dt} \]
  4. Substitute instantaneous snapshot values (\(\frac{dV}{dt} = 3\), \(h = 6\)): \[ 3 = \frac{\pi (6)^2}{9} \frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{36\pi}{9} \frac{dh}{dt} = 4\pi \frac{dh}{dt} \] \[ \frac{dh}{dt} = \mathbf{\frac{3}{4\pi}\text{ m/min}} \approx 0.239\text{ m/min}. \]

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

A 13-foot ladder leans against a vertical wall. The base of the ladder slides away from the wall at a constant rate of 2 ft/s. How fast is the top of the ladder sliding down the wall when the base is 5 feet from the wall?
question.ar:
Level 2 · Medium

A 13-foot ladder leans against a vertical wall. The base of the ladder slides away from the wall at a constant rate of 2 ft/s. How fast is the top of the ladder sliding down the wall عندما the base is 5 feet from the wall?

solution.en:
Let \(x\) be the distance from the base to the wall and \(y\) be the height on the wall. By the Pythagorean theorem: \[ x^2 + y^2 = 13^2 = 169 \] At the instant \(x = 5\): \(y = \sqrt{169 - 25} = \sqrt{144} = 12\text{ ft}\).
Differentiating implicitly with respect to time \(t\): \[ 2x\frac{dx}{dt} + 2y\frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \implies x\frac{dx}{dt} + y\frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \] Substitute \(x = 5\), \(y = 12\), and \(\frac{dx}{dt} = 2\text{ ft/s}\): \[ (5)(2) + (12)\frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \implies 10 + 12\frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \implies \frac{dy}{dt} = -\frac{10}{12} = -\mathbf{\frac{5}{6}\text{ ft/s}}. \] The top of the ladder is sliding down at a rate of \(\frac{5}{6}\text{ ft/s}\) (approx. 0.833 ft/s).

label.en: ● Theorem & Proof: Concavity and Linearization Error
label.ar: ● مبرهنة & برهان: Concavity and Linearization Error

body.en:
Theorem: Let \(f\) be twice differentiable on an open interval \(I\) containing the center of tangency \(a\) and probe point \(x\). Let \(L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a)\) be the local linearization:

  1. If \(f''(t) > 0\) (concave up) for all \(t \in I\), then the tangent line lies below the curve: \[ L(x) < f(x) \quad ( ext{Underestimate for } x eq a) \]
  2. If \(f''(t) < 0\) (concave down) for all \(t \in I\), then the tangent line lies above the curve: \[ L(x) > f(x) \quad ( ext{Overestimate for } x eq a) \]

Proof via Taylor's Theorem with Lagrange Remainder: By Taylor's Theorem, there exists some \(c\) strictly between \(a\) and \(x\) such that: \[ f(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a) + rac{f''(c)}{2!}(x - a)^2 = L(x) + rac{f''(c)}{2}(x - a)^2 \] Subtracting \(L(x)\) yields the exact error formula: \[ f(x) - L(x) = rac{f''(c)}{2}(x - a)^2 \] Since \((x - a)^2 > 0\) for any \(x eq a\), the sign of \(f(x) - L(x)\) is governed solely by the sign of \(f''(c)\). If \(f''(c) < 0\), then \(f(x) - L(x) < 0 \implies L(x) > f(x)\) (overestimate). If \(f''(c) > 0\), then \(f(x) - L(x) > 0 \implies L(x) < f(x)\) (underestimate). \( lacksquare\)

body.en:
Theorem: Suppose \(f\) and \(g\) are differentiable on an open interval containing \(a\) (except possibly at \(a\)), and \(g'(x) \neq 0\) near \(a\). If: \[ \lim_{x\to a} f(x) = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \lim_{x\to a} g(x) = 0 \quad \text{(or } \pm\infty\text{)} \] and the limit \(\lim_{x\to a}\frac{f'(x)}{g'(x)}\) exists or is \(\pm\infty\), then: \[ \lim_{x\to a}\frac{f(x)}{g(x)} = \lim_{x\to a}\frac{f'(x)}{g'(x)} \]

AP Exam Presentation Requirement: College Board AP readers will award zero points for writing \(\lim_{x\to a}\frac{f(x)}{g(x)} = \frac{0}{0}\). You must state the limits of the numerator and denominator separately: \[ \lim_{x\to a} f(x) = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \lim_{x\to a} g(x) = 0 \] state that the indeterminate form is \(\frac{0}{0}\), and then apply L'Hôpital's Rule.

label.ar: Level 3 (Advanced / FRQ) — مثال محلول · Linearization & L'Hôpital Justifications

body.en:
Part A: Let \(f(x) = \sqrt[3]{x}\). Write the equation of the tangent line to \(f\) at \(a = 8\) and use it to approximate \(\sqrt[3]{8.24}\). Explain whether this approximation is an overestimate or underestimate.

Part B: Evaluate \(\displaystyle \lim_{x\to 0} \frac{x - \sin x}{x^3}\) with full AP FRQ limit justifications.

Solution:

Part A: \(f(8) = 2\). The derivative is \(f'(x) = \frac{1}{3}x^{-2/3} = \frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{x^2}}\). At \(x = 8\): \(f'(8) = \frac{1}{3(4)} = \frac{1}{12}\). The linearization is: \[ L(x) = 2 + \frac{1}{12}(x - 8) \] \[ L(8.24) = 2 + \frac{1}{12}(0.24) = 2 + 0.02 = \mathbf{2.02}. \] To determine concavity, find \(f''(x)\): \[ f''(x) = -\frac{2}{9}x^{-5/3} = -\frac{2}{9\sqrt[3]{x^5}} \] For all \(x > 0\), \(f''(x) < 0\), which means \(f\) is concave down. Since the tangent line lies above a concave down curve, \(L(8.24) = 2.02\) is an overestimate.

Part B: Check limits of numerator and denominator separately: \[ \lim_{x\to 0}(x - \sin x) = 0 - 0 = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \lim_{x\to 0} x^3 = 0 \] Since the limit produces the indeterminate form \(\frac{0}{0}\), apply L'Hôpital's Rule: \[ \lim_{x\to 0}\frac{1 - \cos x}{3x^2} \] Check limits again: \(\lim_{x\to 0}(1-\cos x) = 0\) and \(\lim_{x\to 0} 3x^2 = 0\). Apply L'Hôpital's Rule a second time: \[ \lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\sin x}{6x} \] Check limits again: \(\lim_{x\to 0}\sin x = 0\) and \(\lim_{x\to 0} 6x = 0\). Apply L'Hôpital's Rule a third time: \[ \lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\cos x}{6} = \frac{\cos 0}{6} = \mathbf{\frac{1}{6}}. \]

Part B: احسب قيمة \(\displaystyle \lim_{x\to 0} \frac{x - \sin x}{x^3}\) with full AP FRQ النهاية justifications.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

Evaluate the limit: \[ \lim_{x \to 0^+} (\cos x)^{1/x^2} \]
question.ar:
Level 3 · Advanced

احسب قيمة النهاية: \[ \lim_{x \to 0^+} (\cos x)^{1/x^2} \]

solution.en: This is an indeterminate power form of type \(1^\infty\). Let \(y = (\cos x)^{1/x^2}\). Take the natural logarithm: \[ \ln y = \ln\left((\cos x)^{1/x^2}\right) = \frac{\ln(\cos x)}{x^2} \] Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to 0^+} \ln y = \lim_{x\to 0^+} \frac{\ln(\cos x)}{x^2}\). Check limits separately: \(\lim_{x\to 0^+}\ln(\cos x) = \ln 1 = 0\) and \(\lim_{x\to 0^+} x^2 = 0\). Apply L'Hôpital's Rule: \[ \lim_{x\to 0^+} \frac{\frac{-\sin x}{\cos x}}{2x} = \lim_{x\to 0^+} \frac{-\tan x}{2x} = -\frac{1}{2}\lim_{x\to 0^+}\frac{\tan x}{x} = -\frac{1}{2}(1) = -\frac{1}{2}. \] Since \(\lim_{x\to 0^+} \ln y = -\frac{1}{2}\), exponentiate to obtain the original limit: \[ \lim_{x\to 0^+} y = e^{-1/2} = \mathbf{\frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}} \approx 0.6065. \]

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] A rectangular field is to be enclosed by a fence. One side of the field is adjacent to a river and does not require fencing. The farmer has \( 120 \) meters of fencing material. Let the dimensions of the field be \( x \) meters perpendicular to the river and \( y \) meters parallel to the river. The area of the field is given by \( A = xy \). Part A: Express the area \( A \) as a function of \( x \). Part B: Determine the dimensions \( x \) and \( y \) that maximize the area of the field. Provide the maximum possible area.
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Medium] A rectangular field is to be enclosed by a fence. One side of the field is adjacent to a river and does not require fencing. The farmer has \( 120 \) meters of fencing material. ليكن the dimensions of the field be \( x \) meters عمودي على the river and \( y \) meters موازٍ لـ the river. The area of the field is given by \( A = xy \). Part A: Express the area \( A \) as a function of \( x \). Part B: حدّد dimensions \( x \) and \( y \) that maximize the area of the field. Provide the maximum possible area.

hints.en: Part A: The total length of fencing is \( 2x + y = 120 \). Thus, \( y = 120 - 2x \). Substituting this into the area formula, we get \( A(x) = x(120 - 2x) = 120x - 2x^2 \).
hints.ar: Part A: The total length of fencing is \( 2x + y = 120 \). وعليه، \( y = 120 - 2x \). Substituting this into the area formula, we get \( A(x) = x(120 - 2x) = 120x - 2x^2 \).

hints.en: Part B: To find the maximum area, we need to find the critical points of \( A(x) \) by taking the derivative and setting it to zero. \( A'(x) = \frac{dA}{dx} = 120 - 4x \).
hints.ar: Part B: To أوجد maximum area, we need to أوجد critical points of \( A(x) \) by taking the derivative and setting it to zero. \( A'(x) = \frac{dA}{dx} = 120 - 4x \).

hints.en: Therefore, the dimensions that maximize the area are \(x = 30\) m and \(y = 60\) m, with a maximum area of \(1800\) m^2.
hints.ar: وبالتالي، the dimensions that maximize the area are \(x = 30\) m and \(y = 60\) m, with a maximum area of \(1800\) m^2.

solution.en:
Part A: The total length of fencing is \( 2x + y = 120 \). Thus, \( y = 120 - 2x \). Substituting this into the area formula, we get \( A(x) = x(120 - 2x) = 120x - 2x^2 \).

Part B: To find the maximum area, we need to find the critical points of \( A(x) \) by taking the derivative and setting it to zero.
\( A'(x) = \frac{dA}{dx} = 120 - 4x \).
Setting \( A'(x) = 0 \): \( 120 - 4x = 0 \) \( \implies 4x = 120 \) \( \implies x = 30 \) meters.
To confirm this is a maximum, we can use the second derivative test:
\( A''(x) = \frac{d^2A}{dx^2} = -4 \). Since \( A''(30) = -4 < 0 \), the area is maximized at \( x = 30 \) meters.
Now, we find the corresponding \( y \) value:
\( y = 120 - 2x = 120 - 2(30) = 120 - 60 = 60 \) meters.
The maximum area is \( A_{max} = xy = (30)(60) = 1800 \) square meters.
Therefore, the dimensions that maximize the area are \( x = 30 \) m and \( y = 60 \) m, with a maximum area of \( 1800 \) m^2.
solution.ar:
Part A: The total length of fencing is \( 2x + y = 120 \). وعليه، \( y = 120 - 2x \). Substituting this into the area formula, we get \( A(x) = x(120 - 2x) = 120x - 2x^2 \).

Part B: To أوجد maximum area, we need to أوجد critical points of \( A(x) \) by taking the derivative and setting it to zero.
\( A'(x) = \frac{dA}{dx} = 120 - 4x \).
Setting \( A'(x) = 0 \): \( 120 - 4x = 0 \) \( \implies 4x = 120 \) \( \implies x = 30 \) meters.

Now, we أوجد corresponding \( y \) value:

question.en: A rectangular garden has a length that is twice its width. If the perimeter of the garden is 36 meters, what is the width of the garden?
question.ar: A rectangular garden has a length that is twice its width. إذا كان the perimeter of the garden is 36 meters, what is the width of the garden?

hints.en: Let the width of the garden be \( w \) meters.
hints.ar: ليكن the width of the garden be \( w \) meters.

hints.en: According to the problem, the length is twice the width, so the length is \( l = 2w \) meters. The formula for the perimeter of a rectangle is \( P = 2(l + w) \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( l = 2w \) ، \( P = 2(l + w) \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Therefore, the width of the garden is 6 meters.
hints.ar: وبالتالي، the width of the garden is 6 meters.

solution.en:
Let the width of the garden be \( w \) meters. According to the problem, the length is twice the width, so the length is \( l = 2w \) meters. The formula for the perimeter of a rectangle is \( P = 2(l + w) \). We are given that the perimeter is 36 meters. So, we can set up the equation: \( 36 = 2(2w + w) \). Simplifying the equation: \( 36 = 2(3w) \) \( 36 = 6w \). To find the width, divide both sides by 6: \( w = \frac{36}{6} \) \( w = 6 \). Therefore, the width of the garden is 6 meters. 

Common misconceptions:
- Confusing length and width: If one assumed length was width, they might get \( 36 = 2(w + 2w) \), which is the same equation. 
- Incorrect perimeter formula: Using \( P = l \times w \) would lead to \( 36 = 2w \times w = 2w^2 \), so \( w^2 = 18 \), and \( w = \sqrt{18} \), which is not among the options. 
- Calculation error: Dividing 36 by 3 instead of 6 would lead to a width of 12 meters.
solution.ar:
ليكن the width of the garden be \( w \) meters. According to the problem, the length is twice the width, so the length is \( l = 2w \) meters. The formula for the perimeter of a rectangle is \( P = 2(l + w) \). We are إذا علمت أن the perimeter is 36 meters. So, we can set up the equation: \( 36 = 2(2w + w) \). بسّط العبارةing the equation: \( 36 = 2(3w) \) \( 36 = 6w \). To أوجد width, اقسم الطرفين على 6: \( w = \frac{36}{6} \) \( w = 6 \). وبالتالي، the width of the garden is 6 meters. 

Common misconceptions:
- Confusing length and width: إذا كان one assumed length was width, they might get \( 36 = 2(w + 2w) \), which is the same equation.
